# Using Drovr

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this
reflex — it is for the human-facing agent, not for you. Do your task.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

## What this is

This is your **always-on router**. Drovr is a working **discipline**, not just an
orchestration engine, and it is your default operating mode. This skill does not
do the work — it tells you *how* to work and *when* a task has outgrown one
context and must become its own phase.

Drovr exists because model output degrades as a context window fills (Chroma's
*context rot*, trychroma.com/research/context-rot). A fresh, tight context beats
a long one. Everything below serves that.

## The principle (always)

**Single writer, read-only explorers.** One agent edits at a time. Fan-out
investigation goes to read-only explorers (e.g. `explore-mcp`), never to parallel
writers. This holds whether you stay inline or escalate to phases.

**Always review.** Any change you write gets reviewed before you call it done —
invoke **`drovr:code-review`** (read-only review subagents; they find, you fix).
This is not optional and not gated on the change's size; it runs whether you
worked inline or across phases.

## For the task in front of you, apply the right methodology skill

Pick by what you are doing — invoke it via the `Skill` tool before you act:

- Implementing a feature or bugfix → **`drovr:tdd`** (test-first, watch it fail).
- Chasing a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior → **`drovr:systematic-debugging`**.
- About to claim something is done/fixed/passing → **`drovr:verification-before-completion`**.
- Reviewing an artifact (code, spec, plan) → **`drovr:code-review`**. Per the
  *Always review* rule above, this runs on every change — not only before shipping.

## Escalation contract — inline first

**Default: do the work inline in this session.** Do not reach for phases for a
task that fits. Escalate only when a single context cannot hold the work well.

- **Primary signal — context fullness.** If the transcript is filling to the
  point where output would rot, escalate.
- **Secondary heuristic** (a proxy for the above, not a hard rule): roughly
  **10+ files** touched, or **3+ independent work items**.

When you must escalate, pick the smallest tool that fits:

- **Mid-flight escape hatch — author a HANDOFF yourself.** You are deep in a task
  and this context is filling. You have the whole session in context, so compress
  it *yourself*: write a `HANDOFF.md` (the 7-section shape from `drovr:handoff`,
  git pointers included), then continue in a fresh agent seeded from it. Nothing
  compresses it for you — the finishing agent always authors its own handoff.
- **A single planned boundary → `drovr:handoff`.** Hand finished work across one
  phase boundary to a fresh clean-context agent.
- **A full gated run → `drovr:pipeline`.** Brainstorm → plan → implement → review
  with a human approval gate on `spec.md` before any code is written.

**Putting *any* spec/design in front of a human for approval — even a one-off, not a
full pipeline — goes through the review gate, and the gate has two halves you must run
together:** `drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` to present `spec.md`, **and** a
backgrounded `drovr review wait <run>` — the *watch*. (The server itself is global and
always-on: `drovr serve` takes **no** run argument and auto-starts on demand, so serving is not
a step you perform per run.) `summary` opens the gate and prints the reviewer's page URL plus
the exact watch command; it does **not** start the watch. Without the watch you never learn the
decision and fall back to hand-polling `GET /state` (the anti-pattern).
`review wait` blocks on the gate and the harness wakes you when the reviewer acts
(exit `0` approved · `3` request-changes + `feedback.json` · `5` cancelled — the human
abandoned the run, stop · `2` timeout, re-run · `1` error, which is **never** an approval).
Revise loop: edit `spec.md` →
`drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` → re-background `review wait`. Full mechanics
(state machine, diff baselining, gotchas) live in `drovr:pipeline` → "The spec gate".

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** the downstream skills assume this file's contracts —
single-writer rule, the run dir at `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<name>/`, and that
**drovr composes every brief; you supply only context.** `drovr phase start <run>
<phase> --context "<what this phase needs that drovr cannot know>"` composes the
phase's brief and injects it. Never write the frame yourself: `drovr phase brief`
prints what an agent will be told, and `drovr code-review brief … --angle <angle>`
does the same for a reviewer you spawn in-harness. `phase send` remains for
free-form nudges — a message is not a brief.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>",
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart"
  }
}

    /nix/store/fcpab382l1plra0rqbk0dhznmyl1b1xw-kubectl-1.36.2/bin/kubectl --kubeconfig "$BASE" config delete-context "$c" >/dev/null

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- agy-review: Run an independent Gemini review of the current changes via the local Antigravity (`agy`) CLI and surface findings inline in Hunk. Use for "agy review", "gemini review", or a second-opinion / adversarial review of the working-tree diff. NOT for in-harness review — use /code-review for that.
- explain-diff: Use when the user asks for a rich explanation of a code change, diff, branch, or PR.
- hunk-review: Drive a live Hunk diff review session via the `hunk session *` CLI — inspect focus, navigate files/hunks, reload contents, and leave inline review comments. Use when the user has a Hunk session running or wants to walk through / review a diff interactively.
- review-diff: Use when the user wants a rich, annotated review of a code change, diff, branch, or PR — the diff itself organized, annotated, and shown with surrounding codebase context. Complements explain-diff (which teaches); this one is for reviewing.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- slack:channel-digest: Get a digest of recent activity across multiple Slack channels
- slack:draft-announcement: Draft a well-formatted Slack announcement and save it as a draft
- slack:find-discussions: Find discussions about a specific topic across Slack channels
- slack:standup: Generate a standup update based on your recent Slack activity
- slack:summarize-channel: Summarize recent activity in a Slack channel
- drovr:code-review: Use when a drovr phase has produced an artifact (code, spec, plan) and must be reviewed before it is reported done or handed forward
- drovr:handoff: Use when finished work in one agent context must be carried across a phase boundary to a fresh clean-context agent
- drovr:pipeline: Use when a feature or change is too large for one session and needs a human approval gate on its spec before any code is written
- drovr:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior in a drovr phase, before proposing or writing a fix
- drovr:tdd: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix in a drovr phase, before writing implementation code
- drovr:using-drovr: Use at the start of every session as the always-on router — establishes the single-writer discipline, points to the right drovr:* methodology skill for the task, and defines when to escalate a task into its own phase
- drovr:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim a drovr task is done, fixed, or passing, before writing the report or signalling phase done
- drovr:worktrees: Use when deciding whether to isolate a drovr run in its own git worktree, and how to hand its branch back — the discipline behind `drovr new --worktree`
- slack:block-kit: Help developers build and validate Block Kit layouts for Slack messages, modals, and Home tabs. Provides authoritative block references and validates with the blocks.validate API. Use this skill whenever the developer wants to compose Slack message layouts, build modals/forms/dialogs, design Home tab interfaces, create interactive messages with buttons or menus, modify existing Block Kit JSON, or asks about any Slack UI component (sections, actions, inputs, headers, alerts, tables, carousels). Also trigger when they mention "blocks", "Block Kit Builder", want to preview or see the rendered version of blocks, or paste JSON containing block structures like `"type": "section"`.
- slack:create-slack-app: Guide developers through creating a Slack app or agent using the Slack CLI and Bolt (JS or Python). Handles prerequisites, sandbox setup, authentication, project creation from templates, and local development.
- slack:slack-api: Discover, navigate, and call Slack Web API methods (the family.method endpoints at slack.com/api like chat.postMessage, conversations.history, users.info, views.open). Use this skill whenever the developer asks which Slack API method does something, needs a method's required OAuth scopes or token type, wants to call or test a Web API method, is handling cursor pagination (next_cursor), hitting rate limits (tier/ratelimited/Retry-After), or debugging API errors like missing_scope, invalid_auth, or channel_not_found. Also trigger when they paste a slack.com/api/ URL or a docs.slack.dev/reference/methods link, or ask how to list/fetch/post/update Slack resources via the API. This skill covers the Web API method layer: finding the right method, reading its contract (scopes, arguments, errors), and calling it over raw HTTP with curl or through a Slack SDK.
- slack:slack-cli: Use the Slack CLI to create, run, and manage Slack apps from the terminal. Use whenever the developer wants to log in, add a team, switch workspaces, or authenticate with Slack; whenever Slack CLI commands are needed (local development with `slack run`, managing app lifecycle, the manifest).
- slack:slack-docs: Search and read the official Slack platform documentation at docs.slack.dev. Use this skill to answer conceptual or how-to questions about Slack features. You can also use it to look up, fetch, or summarize specific guide pages from provided docs.slack.dev links.
- slack:slack-messaging: Guidance for composing well-formatted, effective Slack messages using standard markdown
- slack:slack-search: Guidance for effectively searching Slack to find messages, files, channels, and people
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.content:
commit 39b97fdd0ee67d044bd4baa9807ff1b53b573917
Author: sauyon <git@sjle.co>
Date:   Tue Jun 9 21:32:25 2026 -0700

    hyprland: port config to Lua (home-manager 26.05 default flip)
    
    home-manager 26.05 changed wayland.windowManager.hyprland.configType to
    default to "lua", which generates ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua via the hl.*
    API instead of a Hyprlang hyprland.conf. The existing Hyprlang-style
    settings didn't translate: $variable definitions became invalid Lua
    (hl.$mainMod(...)), exec-once became hl.exec-once(...), and keyword
    sections / binds / monitors mapped to nonexistent hl.* functions.
    
    Rewrite the config in the Lua-native form, verified with
    `Hyprland --verify-config` (config ok):
    - $mainMod/$terminal/$menu resolved in Nix and inlined
    - general/decoration/animations/input/misc -> hl.config({...})
    - binds -> hl.bind(keys, hl.dsp.exec_cmd/exec_raw(...), opts); mouse
      drag/resize use hl.dsp.window.drag()/resize() with { mouse = true }
    - monitor/workspace_rule/device -> table specs; env -> two args
    - exec-once -> hl.on("hyprland.start", ...) (D-Bus/systemd hook is
      emitted by the module itself)
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
Diagnosis done. Your Hyprland config is **not** the problem — it's applied correctly at runtime (verified: `gaps_in=0`, animations off, Framework keyboard on `colemak`).

## Root cause: your systemd **user manager** has `HOME=/`

```
$ systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath
UnitPath=/.config/systemd/user      ← should be /home/sauyon/.config/systemd/user
$ systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME
HOME=/
```

So systemd searches `/.config/systemd/user` and **cannot see a single home-manager user unit**, even though all ~30 symlinks exist in `~/.config/systemd/user/`:

```
$ systemctl --user status waybar
Unit waybar.service could not be found.
```

Both your symptoms are the same bug:

| Symptom | Dead unit |
|---|---|
| No waybar | `waybar.service` (you have `systemd.enable = true`) |
| Monitors wrong | `kanshi.service` — the `Modular` profile (Dell P3424WEB at `-528,-1440`, laptop at `0,0`) never applies, so Hyprland falls back to its catch-all `position = "auto"` → eDP-1 at `0x0`, DP-5 at `2560x0`, side by side |

Also dead for the same reason: `hypridle`, `hyprpaper`, `walker`, `ssh-tpm-agent`, `sops-nix`, the xdg portals.

**Why `HOME=/`:** `sauyon` is a systemd-homed LUKS user (`/home/sauyon.home`, uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`). The manager (pid 2107) started `Jul 30 21:52:32`, 2m14s after boot, triggered by a `Service=remote` session — before the encrypted home was resolvable. UnitPath is computed once at manager start, so it's been wrong for this entire 17-hour boot.

---
name: project_tailscale_ssh_poisons_user_manager
description: On utsuho, an early Tailscale SSH login starts systemd --user with HOME=/ before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot
metadata:
  type: project
---

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), an inbound **Tailscale SSH** connection that lands before
Sauyon logs in physically permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. Tailscale SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>`
   → PAM service **`remote`** (`Service=remote` in `loginctl show-session`).
2. `login -f` **skips the PAM auth stack**, so `pam_systemd_home.so` (auth, `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6`)
   never runs → the LUKS home is never unlocked.
3. `pam_systemd.so` (session, `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20`) still runs → logind creates
   the session → starts `user@60006.service`.
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `systemd --user` gets **`HOME=/`** → its unit search
   path becomes `/.config/systemd/user`. UnitPath is computed **once at manager start**,
   so it stays poisoned for the entire boot even after the home later unlocks.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**This is a Tailscale SSH interaction bug, not a systemd bug** — systemd's `HOME=/`
fallback and start-time UnitPath are by design.

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Workaround (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
Real fix: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service` restarts with the home
mounted — or stop Tailscale SSH from creating a session before first physical login.

Related: [[project_hyprlock_pam_auth]], [[feedback_always_run_hm_switch]]

description: "On utsuho, an early Tailscale SSH login starts systemd --user with HOME=/ before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot"

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), an inbound **Tailscale SSH** connection that lands before
Sauyon logs in physically permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. Tailscale SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>`
   → PAM service **`remote`** (`Service=remote` in `loginctl show-session`).
2. `login -f` **skips the PAM auth stack**, so `pam_systemd_home.so` (auth, `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6`)
   never runs → the LUKS home is never unlocked.
3. `pam_systemd.so` (session, `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20`) still runs → logind creates
   the session → starts `user@60006.service`.
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `systemd --user` gets **`HOME=/`** → its unit search
   path becomes `/.config/systemd/user`. UnitPath is computed **once at manager start**,
   so it stays poisoned for the entire boot even after the home later unlocks.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**This is a Tailscale SSH interaction bug, not a systemd bug** — systemd's `HOME=/`
fallback and start-time UnitPath are by design.

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Workaround (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
Real fix: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service` restarts with the home
mounted — or stop Tailscale SSH from creating a session before first physical login.

Related: [[project_hyprlock_pam_auth]], [[feedback_always_run_hm_switch]]

content.text:
**Tailscale SSH bug**, not a systemd bug. Both symptoms are fixed live.

## Fixed now

1. **waybar** — running (pid 929869), both bars up on eDP-1 and DP-5
2. **monitors** — kanshi applied the `Modular` profile: DP-5 now at `-528x-1440`, eDP-1 at `0x0`

## Why it's Tailscale's fault

Traced the exact PAM path:

1. TS SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>` → PAM service **`remote`** (matches `Service=remote` on your pts/0 session, Jul 30 21:52)
2. `login -f` **skips the auth stack** → `pam_systemd_home.so` at `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6` never runs → your LUKS home is never unlocked
3. `pam_systemd.so` at `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20` *does* run → logind creates the session → starts `user@60006.service`
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `HOME=/` → UnitPath = `/.config/systemd/user`

systemd's side is all by-design: `HOME=/` is the documented fallback, and UnitPath is computed once at manager start — so it stayed poisoned for all 17 hours of this boot, even after you unlocked at 16:50 today. Tailscale is the one creating a logind session for a systemd-homed user without unlocking the home.

## What didn't work

`systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec` — no effect. `set-environment` only changes the env handed to child units; the manager re-execs with its own unchanged `environ`.

## Still broken until you log out

waybar and kanshi are unsupervised processes, not units. These remain dead: `hypridle`, `hyprpaper`, `walker`, `ssh-tpm-agent`, `sops-nix`, xdg portals. A full logout of **all** sessions restarts `user@60006.service` with the home mounted and fixes everything permanently for that boot.

I made no changes to the dotfiles repo — nothing to commit.

**Next (2 min):** run `tailscale set --ssh=false` if you don't rely on inbound TS SSH to utsuho — that removes the trigger entirely and is the only durable fix short of a PAM change.

content.content:
# Tailscale SSH PAM Session Issue

Based on the GitHub issue #13198, the problem is that **PAM sessions are not being opened when users connect via SSH through Tailscale**.

## The Core Problem

When connecting via Tailscale SSH, users are missing critical session initialization, as evidenced by:
- The `loginuid` showing `4294967295` (unset)
- Users not appearing in `wtmp` logs
- No `logind` session being created
- Session IDs marked with "c" prefix in `loginctl` output

## Impact

This causes several issues:
- **Auditing failures**: Login information isn't properly recorded
- **SELinux complications**: Users don't run in the proper security context
- **Session tracking**: No proper accounting of who's logged in

## Current Status

The issue was opened on August 20, 2024, and remains listed as a bug without assignment, suggesting it hasn't been resolved. The issue doesn't provide workarounds or configuration options in the visible content.

The underlying question—whether Tailscale SSH actually executes the full PAM stack (auth/account/session phases)—appears to be the root cause, though the page doesn't explicitly detail Tailscale's PAM handling implementation.

content.content:
# Tailscale SSH Incubator Process on Linux

Based on the documentation provided:

## Session Startup Method

The incubator uses **direct execution** rather than `login` or `su`. It spawns itself with `"be-child ssh"` subcommand to handle privilege separation.

## PAM Integration

The system does **not call PAM directly**. However, it relies on PAM indirectly through `pam_mkhomedir`, which the testing infrastructure validates on Ubuntu systems to ensure home directories are created during session initialization.

## Systemd-logind Registration

Yes, the incubator **registers sessions with systemd-logind via D-Bus**. Specifically, on Linux it registers with `"org.freedesktop.login1"` to establish proper login session tracking.

## Privilege Dropping

The process implements security-critical privilege dropping with "defensive assertions to ensure privileges cannot be re-escalated." When direct home directory access fails, the implementation includes a fallback mechanism that executes the login shell instead.

## Summary

The incubator combines direct command execution with systemd-logind D-Bus integration for session management, PAM-based home directory creation (where available), and explicit privilege-dropping mechanisms—providing proper authentication and session isolation without invoking traditional login utilities.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-oomd

# ── attic binary cache: make nix read nix.custom.conf + render the pull token ──
# nix.custom.conf adds attic.ko.ag/kube as an extra substituter; the cache is
# PRIVATE, so the nix daemon needs a read token. We are not a nix `trusted-user`,
# so both the config and the token must reach the daemon at the system level.
#
#   • Determinate Nix auto-`!include`s nix.custom.conf from /etc/nix/nix.conf and
#     merges /etc/determinate/netrc.custom (via config.json) into its netrc.
#   • Plain upstream nix (e.g. utsuho) does neither, so we wire it up here:
#       - ensure /etc/nix/nix.conf `!include`s nix.custom.conf (idempotent)
#       - render the token to /etc/nix/netrc, the daemon's default netrc-file
#     (On a Determinate host the extra /etc/nix/netrc copy is simply unused.)
# The token is sops-encrypted in ../secrets.yaml: decrypt as the user (GCP KMS),
# then install to /etc as root. The token is never printed.
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="${GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS:-$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json}"

# Plain upstream nix only reads /etc/nix/nix.conf; pull in nix.custom.conf so the
# substituter + trusted key take effect. Idempotent, and a no-op on Determinate
# (whose own nix.conf already includes it, so the grep matches and we skip).
if ! sudo grep -qF 'nix.custom.conf' /etc/nix/nix.conf 2>/dev/null; then
  echo '!include nix.custom.conf' | sudo tee -a /etc/nix/nix.conf >/dev/null
fi

sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/determinate/netrc.custom
sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/netrc

# ── remote builder: SSH key the nix daemon uses to reach mari ─────────────────
# nix.custom.conf delegates aarch64-darwin builds to sauyon@mari-1 over Tailscale;
# the daemon (root) authenticates with this key. Private key is sops-encrypted in
# ../secrets.yaml; install root-owned, 0600. Never printed.
sops -d --extract '["mariBuilderKey"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/mari-builder-key

# Pick up the new substituter, trusted key, netrc, and builder.
sudo systemctl restart nix-daemon

# Pin HOME for sauyon's systemd user manager.
#
# `sauyon` is a systemd-homed user whose home is a LUKS image (/home/sauyon.home),
# so it does not exist until someone authenticates with a password. Any *passwordless*
# login that lands before that — Tailscale SSH (`Service=tailscaled`, registered
# straight with logind over D-Bus) or a key-based remote login (`Service=remote`) —
# makes logind start user@60006.service while the home is still locked.
#
# user@.service has `User=%i`, so systemd derives HOME from the user record; with the
# home unusable it falls back to HOME=/. systemd computes the user unit search path
# ONCE at manager startup, so it becomes /.config/systemd/user and stays that way for
# the entire boot. Every home-manager user unit is then invisible:
#
#   $ systemctl --user status waybar
#   Unit waybar.service could not be found.
#
# Symptoms: no waybar, kanshi never applies its monitor profile, hypridle/hyprpaper/
# walker/ssh-tpm-agent/sops-nix/xdg-portals all dead, and `home-manager switch` aborts
# at "Activating sops-nix" (silently skipping every later activation step).
#
# PAM is NOT the missing piece. /usr/lib/pam.d/systemd-user already includes
# system-auth in its session phase, which already runs `pam_systemd_home.so`. That
# module can only *reference* an already-active home — activating a LUKS home needs
# the password, and none of these logins have one. Tailscale SSH additionally skips
# PAM entirely (tailscale/tailscale#13198), and exposes no option to change that.
#
# So pin HOME explicitly. Environment= takes precedence over the User=-derived value
# (verified: systemd-run -p User=sauyon -p Environment=HOME=/tmp/hometest -> /tmp/hometest),
# which makes the search path correct from the first instant regardless of mount state.
# If the manager still starts before the home is unlocked the path is right but empty;
# a later `systemctl --user daemon-reload` (which home-manager activation runs anyway)
# then picks up every unit — instead of requiring a full logout.
#
# Takes effect on the next start of user@60006.service: a full logout of all sessions,
# or a reboot.
[Service]
Environment=HOME=/home/sauyon

name: project_tailscale_ssh_poisons_user_manager
description: "On utsuho, an early Tailscale SSH login starts systemd --user with HOME=/ before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0128a5ea-fdfb-4809-a8c9-e357b740dc41
  modified: 2026-08-01T03:29:11.544Z
---

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), an inbound **Tailscale SSH** connection that lands before
Sauyon logs in physically permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. Tailscale SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>`
   → PAM service **`remote`** (`Service=remote` in `loginctl show-session`).
2. `login -f` **skips the PAM auth stack**, so `pam_systemd_home.so` (auth, `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6`)
   never runs → the LUKS home is never unlocked.
3. `pam_systemd.so` (session, `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20`) still runs → logind creates
   the session → starts `user@60006.service`.
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `systemd --user` gets **`HOME=/`** → its unit search
   path becomes `/.config/systemd/user`. UnitPath is computed **once at manager start**,
   so it stays poisoned for the entire boot even after the home later unlocks.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**This is a Tailscale SSH interaction bug, not a systemd bug** — systemd's `HOME=/`
fallback and start-time UnitPath are by design.

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Also presents as **`home-manager switch` failing**: activation aborts at
`Activating sops-nix` with "Failed to restart sops-nix.service: Unit sops-nix.service
not found", which **silently skips every later activation step** (on utsuho:
`opencodeConfig`, `patchOpencodeModelStats`, `reloadSystemd`) — so `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
keeps its stale/unkeyed contents. Recover without logging out (verified 2026-07-31):

1. Render the secrets by running the unit's `ExecStart` by hand with a clean env —
   `env -i HOME=/home/sauyon USER=sauyon XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60006
   GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json PATH=
   $(grep ExecStart= <the sops-nix.service unit> | cut -d= -f2-)`.

2. Run the skipped tail of `$(readlink -f ~/.local/state/nix/profiles/home-manager)/activate`
   under `bash` (not zsh — the script uses bash arrays) with `DRY_RUN_CMD=` and a stub
   `_iNote`. Skip `reloadSystemd`; it is a no-op while the manager is poisoned.

Workaround for GUI units (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.

mounted — or stop Tailscale SSH from creating a session before first physical login.

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), any **passwordless login that lands before Sauyon
authenticates physically** permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. The LUKS home does not exist until someone supplies the password. A passwordless
   login still makes logind create a session, which starts `user@60006.service`.
2. `user@.service` has `User=%i`, so systemd derives HOME from the user record. The home
   is unusable, so it falls back to **`HOME=/`**.
3. systemd computes the user unit search path **once at manager startup** → it becomes
   `/.config/systemd/user` and stays wrong for the entire boot, even after the home unlocks.

CORRECTION (verified 2026-08-02) — an earlier version of this note blamed Tailscale SSH
running `login -f` under PAM service `remote`. **That was wrong.** Check `Service=` in
`loginctl show-session <id>`:
- Tailscale SSH sessions are the **`c`-prefixed** ones with **`Service=tailscaled`** —
  registered straight with logind over D-Bus, skipping PAM entirely
  (tailscale/tailscale#13198, open since 2024-08; no flag to change it — 1.98.9 has only
  a boolean `--ssh`).
- **`Service=remote`** sessions are a *different*, non-Tailscale remote login (util-linux
  `login -h`, e.g. mosh). So disabling Tailscale SSH would NOT be sufficient.
The exact trigger at boot was unrecoverable — the early system journal had already been
vacuumed (this boot logged >9M `_UID=0` lines).

**"Just make it run PAM" does not work, and PAM already runs.** `user@.service` sets

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), an inbound **Tailscale SSH** connection that lands before
Sauyon logs in physically permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. Tailscale SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>`
   → PAM service **`remote`** (`Service=remote` in `loginctl show-session`).
2. `login -f` **skips the PAM auth stack**, so `pam_systemd_home.so` (auth, `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6`)
   never runs → the LUKS home is never unlocked.
3. `pam_systemd.so` (session, `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20`) still runs → logind creates
   the session → starts `user@60006.service`.
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `systemd --user` gets **`HOME=/`** → its unit search
   path becomes `/.config/systemd/user`. UnitPath is computed **once at manager start**,
   so it stays poisoned for the entire boot even after the home later unlocks.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**This is a Tailscale SSH interaction bug, not a systemd bug** — systemd's `HOME=/`
fallback and start-time UnitPath are by design.

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Also presents as **`home-manager switch` failing**: activation aborts at
`Activating sops-nix` with "Failed to restart sops-nix.service: Unit sops-nix.service
not found", which **silently skips every later activation step** (on utsuho:
`opencodeConfig`, `patchOpencodeModelStats`, `reloadSystemd`) — so `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
keeps its stale/unkeyed contents. Recover without logging out (verified 2026-07-31):

1. Render the secrets by running the unit's `ExecStart` by hand with a clean env —
   `env -i HOME=/home/sauyon USER=sauyon XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60006
   GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json PATH=
   $(grep ExecStart= <the sops-nix.service unit> | cut -d= -f2-)`.
   It bumps `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d/<n>` and repoints `~/.config/sops-nix/secrets`.
2. Run the skipped tail of `$(readlink -f ~/.local/state/nix/profiles/home-manager)/activate`
   under `bash` (not zsh — the script uses bash arrays) with `DRY_RUN_CMD=` and a stub
   `_iNote`. Skip `reloadSystemd`; it is a no-op while the manager is poisoned.

Workaround for GUI units (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
Real fix: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service` restarts with the home
mounted — or stop Tailscale SSH from creating a session before first physical login.

Related: [[project_hyprlock_pam_auth]], [[feedback_always_run_hm_switch]]

---
name: project_tailscale_ssh_poisons_user_manager
description: "On utsuho, an early Tailscale SSH login starts systemd --user with HOME=/ before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0128a5ea-fdfb-4809-a8c9-e357b740dc41
  modified: 2026-08-02T07:08:26.156Z
---

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), any **passwordless login that lands before Sauyon
authenticates physically** permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. The LUKS home does not exist until someone supplies the password. A passwordless
   login still makes logind create a session, which starts `user@60006.service`.
2. `user@.service` has `User=%i`, so systemd derives HOME from the user record. The home
   is unusable, so it falls back to **`HOME=/`**.
3. systemd computes the user unit search path **once at manager startup** → it becomes
   `/.config/systemd/user` and stays wrong for the entire boot, even after the home unlocks.

CORRECTION (verified 2026-08-02) — an earlier version of this note blamed Tailscale SSH
running `login -f` under PAM service `remote`. **That was wrong.** Check `Service=` in
`loginctl show-session <id>`:
- Tailscale SSH sessions are the **`c`-prefixed** ones with **`Service=tailscaled`** —
  registered straight with logind over D-Bus, skipping PAM entirely
  (tailscale/tailscale#13198, open since 2024-08; no flag to change it — 1.98.9 has only
  a boolean `--ssh`).
- **`Service=remote`** sessions are a *different*, non-Tailscale remote login (util-linux
  `login -h`, e.g. mosh). So disabling Tailscale SSH would NOT be sufficient.
The exact trigger at boot was unrecoverable — the early system journal had already been
vacuumed (this boot logged >9M `_UID=0` lines).

**"Just make it run PAM" does not work, and PAM already runs.** `user@.service` sets
`PAMName=systemd-user`; `/usr/lib/pam.d/systemd-user` (NOT `/etc/pam.d/`) includes
`system-auth` in its **session** phase, which already runs `pam_systemd_home.so`. That
module can only *reference* an already-active home — **activating a LUKS home requires the
password**, and passwordless logins have none. More PAM cannot fix this.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**THE FIX** (in the dotfiles repo, deployed by `system/deploy`):
`system/etc/systemd/system/user@60006.service.d/10-home.conf` → `Environment=HOME=/home/sauyon`.
`Environment=` takes precedence over the `User=`-derived HOME — verified with
`sudo systemd-run --wait --pipe -p User=sauyon -p Environment=HOME=/tmp/hometest
sh -c 'echo $HOME'` → `/tmp/hometest`. This makes the search path correct from the first
instant regardless of mount state; if the manager still starts pre-unlock the path is
right but empty, and a later `systemctl --user daemon-reload` picks up every unit instead
of needing a full logout. Only takes effect on the next start of `user@60006.service`
(full logout of all sessions, or reboot).

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Also presents as **`home-manager switch` failing**: activation aborts at
`Activating sops-nix` with "Failed to restart sops-nix.service: Unit sops-nix.service
not found", which **silently skips every later activation step** (on utsuho:
`opencodeConfig`, `patchOpencodeModelStats`, `reloadSystemd`) — so `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
keeps its stale/unkeyed contents. Recover without logging out (verified 2026-07-31):

1. Render the secrets by running the unit's `ExecStart` by hand with a clean env —
   `env -i HOME=/home/sauyon USER=sauyon XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60006
   GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json PATH=
   $(grep ExecStart= <the sops-nix.service unit> | cut -d= -f2-)`.
   It bumps `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d/<n>` and repoints `~/.config/sops-nix/secrets`.
2. Run the skipped tail of `$(readlink -f ~/.local/state/nix/profiles/home-manager)/activate`
   under `bash` (not zsh — the script uses bash arrays) with `DRY_RUN_CMD=` and a stub
   `_iNote`. Skip `reloadSystemd`; it is a no-op while the manager is poisoned.

Workaround for GUI units (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
To recover the *current* boot: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service`
restarts with the home mounted. (The drop-in above prevents recurrence but cannot repair
a manager that is already running.)

Related: [[project_hyprlock_pam_auth]], [[feedback_always_run_hm_switch]]

git add -A && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git push -q origin master && echo "PUSHED"
system: pin HOME for sauyon's systemd user manager

`sauyon` is a systemd-homed user whose home is a LUKS image, so it does not
exist until someone authenticates with a password. Any passwordless login that
lands first (Tailscale SSH, or a key-based remote login) makes logind start
user@60006.service while the home is still locked.

user@.service has `User=%i`, so systemd derives HOME from the user record and
falls back to HOME=/ when the home is unusable. The user unit search path is
computed once at manager startup, so it becomes /.config/systemd/user and stays
wrong for the whole boot -- every home-manager user unit goes invisible. That
presents as "hyprland is broken" (no waybar, kanshi never applies its monitor
profile) and as `home-manager switch` aborting at "Activating sops-nix".

PAM is not the missing piece: user@.service already sets PAMName=systemd-user,
and /usr/lib/pam.d/systemd-user already includes system-auth in its session
phase, which already runs pam_systemd_home.so. That module can only reference an
already-active home -- activating a LUKS home needs the password, which none of
these logins have. Tailscale SSH additionally bypasses PAM entirely
(tailscale/tailscale#13198) with no option to change it.

So pin HOME explicitly. Environment= takes precedence over the User=-derived
value, verified with:

  sudo systemd-run --wait --pipe -p User=sauyon \
    -p Environment=HOME=/tmp/hometest sh -c 'echo $HOME'   # -> /tmp/hometest

Takes effect on the next start of user@60006.service.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
Done — but not the way you asked, because the PAM route can't work. Here's why, with the evidence.

## PAM already runs. That's not the missing piece.

`user@.service` sets `PAMName=systemd-user`, and the stack lives at **`/usr/lib/pam.d/systemd-user`** (not `/etc/pam.d/`, which is why it looked absent):

```
session    include    system-auth     ← and system-auth:24 is:
                                         -session optional pam_systemd_home.so
```

So `pam_systemd_home` **is already being invoked** for your user manager, and you still got `HOME=/`. The reason is structural: that module can only take a reference to an *already-active* home. Activating a LUKS home needs the **password**, and every login that trips this is passwordless (tailnet identity, SSH key). No PAM configuration produces a password that isn't there.

## Two corrections to what I told you Friday

1. **`login -f` / PAM service `remote` was wrong.** `Service=` proves it — your Tailscale SSH sessions are the `c`-prefixed ones with `Service=tailscaled`, registered straight with logind over D-Bus, bypassing PAM entirely ([tailscale#13198](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/13198), open since Aug 2024; [incubator design](https://deepwiki.com/tailscale/tailscale/7.2-ssh-server-(tailscale-ssh))). The `Service=remote` session at boot was something *else* remote (util-linux `login -h`, e.g. mosh). So disabling Tailscale SSH would not have been sufficient either.
2. **The exact boot trigger is unrecoverable.** The early system journal was already vacuumed — this boot has logged >9M `_UID=0` lines.

## What I did instead

Pinned `HOME` on the manager itself — `system/etc/systemd/system/user@60006.service.d/10-home.conf`:

```ini
[Service]
Environment=HOME=/home/sauyon
```

Verified the precedence empirically before relying on it:

```
$ sudo systemd-run --wait --pipe -p User=sauyon -p Environment=HOME=/tmp/hometest sh -c 'echo $HOME'
HOME=/tmp/hometest      ← Environment= beats the User=-derived HOME
```

1. Committed + pushed (`9faca06`) — needed a rebase, remote had two newer commits
2. Installed to `/etc` and `daemon-reload`ed; `systemctl show user@60006.service -p Environment` → `Environment=HOME=/home/sauyon`

Now the search path is correct from the first instant regardless of mount state. If the manager still starts pre-unlock, the path is right but empty, and any later `systemctl --user daemon-reload` picks up every unit — instead of a mandatory logout.

Also: I misread `pgrep -x` and reported waybar dead when it wasn't, started a duplicate, and killed the one I started. You're back to one waybar (929869) and kanshi still running.

**This boot is still poisoned** — the drop-in only applies to the next start of `user@60006.service`.

**Next (~1 min):** log out of *all* sessions (or reboot) — that's the only thing that clears the current manager, and on the way back up the drop-in takes over. Verify with `systemctl --user show -p UnitPath | tr ' ' '\n' | grep sauyon`.

Sources: [tailscale/tailscale#13198](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/13198) · [Tailscale SSH incubator (DeepWiki)](https://deepwiki.com/tailscale/tailscale/7.2-ssh-server-(tailscale-ssh))

input.prompt: What do the fields fallbackHomeDirectory, fallbackShell and useFallback mean? When is fallbackHomeDirectory used instead of homeDirectory? Does systemd-homed withhold or change the reported home directory when a user's home is NOT active/unlocked? Quote the relevant passages.

content.content:
# Fallback Fields Usage

The `fallbackHomeDirectory`, `fallbackShell`, and `useFallback` fields are mechanisms for handling scenarios where a user's home directory requires additional unlocking.

## When Fallback Fields Are Used

According to the specification: "When the `useFallback` field is set to true, the data from these fields should override the fields of the same name without the `fallback` prefix."

## The Specific Use Case

The document explains the context: "This mechanism is used for enable subsystems such as SSH to allow logins into user accounts, whose homed directories need further unlocking (because the SSH native authentication cannot release a suitable disk encryption key), which the fallback shell provides."

In essence, when a user's encrypted home directory cannot be automatically unlocked through the standard authentication mechanism (particularly via SSH), the system switches to fallback values by setting `useFallback` to `true`. This allows the login to proceed using an alternative shell and home directory path, providing a degraded but functional login experience until the primary home directory can be properly unlocked.

The fallback fields exist in the `status` section, meaning they are runtime-only values that reflect the current system state rather than persistent user configuration.

## Key Findings:

**useFallback and fallbackHomeDirectory**: The fallbackShell and fallbackHomeDirectory fields have the same contents and format as the shell and homeDirectory fields, and when the useFallback field is set to true, the data from these fields should override the fields of the same name. This mechanism is used for enable subsystems such as SSH to allow logins into user accounts, whose homed directories need further unlocking (because the SSH native authentication cannot release a suitable disk encryption key), which the fallback shell provides.

The results also suggest that when using user-specific services with systemd-homed, the correct placement of unit files in `~/.config/systemd/user/` and proper configuration is essential, though the specific "user@.service" path issue you're asking about would require more detailed investigation in the actual GitHub issue tracker.

# Issue Summary

This GitHub issue reports that user-defined systemd units stored in `~/.config/systemd/user/` are silently ignored when systemd-homed is in use, though the same units work fine without homed on the same system.

## Key Details

**The Problem:**
The reporter notes that systemd cannot locate custom service files in the user configuration directory when homed is active. Interestingly, `systemd-analyze verify` can validate the unit files, indicating they're readable but not discoverable by systemctl.

**Reproduction Method:**
The issue occurs specifically with "systemd-homed with standard Btrfs subvolume mounts" but disappears when using the identical OS and systemd version without homed enabled.

## Status & Resolution

**Current Status:** The issue was closed as a duplicate of [#34151](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/34151), suggesting this is a known, related problem within the systemd project.

The web content provided doesn't specify the root cause, available workarounds, or merged fixes. To find solutions, you'd need to examine issue #34151 or related systemd-homed documentation regarding unit file discovery paths and Btrfs subvolume handling.

content.content:
# Summary of GitHub Issue #30727

## Overview
This issue reports that systemd user units fail to activate approximately 50% of the time after reboots when using systemd-homed, despite being marked as enabled.

## Root Cause
The journal logs reveal permission denied errors when systemd tries to access user configuration directories:

> "Failed to open "/home/mralexandernickel/.config/systemd/user", ignoring: Permission denied"

The core problem appears to be a **timing issue where the user daemon attempts to load units before the homed container has fully mounted the home directory**, resulting in inaccessible configuration paths.

## Key Details
- **Affected System**: Arch Linux with systemd 255
- **Reproduction**: Create a homed user, enable simple units (timers/services), then reboot multiple times
- **Pattern**: The issue occurs inconsistently; regular (non-homed) users don't experience this problem
- **Additional Errors**: Permission failures also affect podman and XDG autostart generators

## Status
The issue remains **open** with labels indicating it needs reporter feedback and involves both the homed and pid1 (systemd core) components. No merged pull requests are mentioned in the provided content.

## Workaround
The document doesn't explicitly suggest workarounds, though the contrast with working non-homed accounts suggests potential timing or mount ordering issues.

input.old_string:
Mechanism:
1. The LUKS home does not exist until someone supplies the password. A passwordless
   login still makes logind create a session, which starts `user@60006.service`.
2. `user@.service` has `User=%i`, so systemd derives HOME from the user record. The home
   is unusable, so it falls back to **`HOME=/`**.
3. systemd computes the user unit search path **once at manager startup** → it becomes
   `/.config/systemd/user` and stays wrong for the entire boot, even after the home unlocks.
input.new_string:
Mechanism — **`HOME=/` is explicit systemd-homed design, not an accident**:
1. The LUKS home cannot be unlocked without the password. When a login can't release the
   encryption key, homed sets **`useFallback: true`** in the *status* section of the user
   record, which makes `fallbackHomeDirectory` and `fallbackShell` override the real ones.
   On utsuho (`userdbctl user sauyon --json=pretty`):
   `"fallbackHomeDirectory": "/"`, `"fallbackShell": "/usr/bin/systemd-home-fallback-shell"`
   (a symlink to `homectl`). Documented in systemd `docs/USER_RECORD.md` — the stated purpose
   is to let subsystems "such as SSH" log into accounts whose home needs further unlocking.
2. That passwordless login still makes logind start `user@60006.service`, which has
   `User=%i` → systemd takes the *fallback* home → **`HOME=/`**.
3. systemd computes the user unit search path **once at manager startup** → it becomes
   `/.config/systemd/user` and stays wrong for the entire boot, even after the home unlocks
   and `useFallback` flips back to `false`.

The real defect: `useFallback` is scoped to a **login session**, but it gets baked into
`user@<uid>.service`, which is **boot-scoped** and never re-evaluated. Known open upstream
bug: systemd/systemd#30727 (labels homed + pid1, still open) and #36769 (closed as dup of
#34151). NOT a generic "home missing → `/`" fallback: verified that systemd happily sets
`HOME=/usr/share/empty` for user `passim` whose home does not exist.

name: project_tailscale_ssh_poisons_user_manager
description: "On utsuho, any passwordless login landing before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks starts systemd --user with HOME=/, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot; fixed by a user@60006.service.d drop-in pinning HOME"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0128a5ea-fdfb-4809-a8c9-e357b740dc41
  modified: 2026-08-02T07:08:33.412Z
---

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), any **passwordless login that lands before Sauyon
authenticates physically** permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. The LUKS home does not exist until someone supplies the password. A passwordless
   login still makes logind create a session, which starts `user@60006.service`.
2. `user@.service` has `User=%i`, so systemd derives HOME from the user record. The home
   is unusable, so it falls back to **`HOME=/`**.
3. systemd computes the user unit search path **once at manager startup** → it becomes
   `/.config/systemd/user` and stays wrong for the entire boot, even after the home unlocks.

CORRECTION (verified 2026-08-02) — an earlier version of this note blamed Tailscale SSH
running `login -f` under PAM service `remote`. **That was wrong.** Check `Service=` in
`loginctl show-session <id>`:
- Tailscale SSH sessions are the **`c`-prefixed** ones with **`Service=tailscaled`** —
  registered straight with logind over D-Bus, skipping PAM entirely
  (tailscale/tailscale#13198, open since 2024-08; no flag to change it — 1.98.9 has only
  a boolean `--ssh`).
- **`Service=remote`** sessions are a *different*, non-Tailscale remote login (util-linux
  `login -h`, e.g. mosh). So disabling Tailscale SSH would NOT be sufficient.
The exact trigger at boot was unrecoverable — the early system journal had already been
vacuumed (this boot logged >9M `_UID=0` lines).

**"Just make it run PAM" does not work, and PAM already runs.** `user@.service` sets
`PAMName=systemd-user`; `/usr/lib/pam.d/systemd-user` (NOT `/etc/pam.d/`) includes
`system-auth` in its **session** phase, which already runs `pam_systemd_home.so`. That
module can only *reference* an already-active home — **activating a LUKS home requires the
password**, and passwordless logins have none. More PAM cannot fix this.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**THE FIX** (in the dotfiles repo, deployed by `system/deploy`):
`system/etc/systemd/system/user@60006.service.d/10-home.conf` → `Environment=HOME=/home/sauyon`.
`Environment=` takes precedence over the `User=`-derived HOME — verified with
`sudo systemd-run --wait --pipe -p User=sauyon -p Environment=HOME=/tmp/hometest
sh -c 'echo $HOME'` → `/tmp/hometest`. This makes the search path correct from the first
instant regardless of mount state; if the manager still starts pre-unlock the path is
right but empty, and a later `systemctl --user daemon-reload` picks up every unit instead
of needing a full logout. Only takes effect on the next start of `user@60006.service`
(full logout of all sessions, or reboot).

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Also presents as **`home-manager switch` failing**: activation aborts at
`Activating sops-nix` with "Failed to restart sops-nix.service: Unit sops-nix.service
not found", which **silently skips every later activation step** (on utsuho:
`opencodeConfig`, `patchOpencodeModelStats`, `reloadSystemd`) — so `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
keeps its stale/unkeyed contents. Recover without logging out (verified 2026-07-31):

1. Render the secrets by running the unit's `ExecStart` by hand with a clean env —
   `env -i HOME=/home/sauyon USER=sauyon XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60006
   GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json PATH=
   $(grep ExecStart= <the sops-nix.service unit> | cut -d= -f2-)`.
   It bumps `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d/<n>` and repoints `~/.config/sops-nix/secrets`.
2. Run the skipped tail of `$(readlink -f ~/.local/state/nix/profiles/home-manager)/activate`
   under `bash` (not zsh — the script uses bash arrays) with `DRY_RUN_CMD=` and a stub
   `_iNote`. Skip `reloadSystemd`; it is a no-op while the manager is poisoned.

Workaround for GUI units (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
To recover the *current* boot: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service`
restarts with the home mounted. (The drop-in above prevents recurrence but cannot repair
a manager that is already running.)

Related: [[project_hyprlock_pam_auth]], [[feedback_always_run_hm_switch]]

**"Just make it run PAM" does not work, and PAM already runs.** `user@.service` sets
`PAMName=systemd-user`; `/usr/lib/pam.d/systemd-user` (NOT `/etc/pam.d/`) includes
`system-auth` in its **session** phase, which already runs `pam_systemd_home.so`. That
module can only *reference* an already-active home — **activating a LUKS home requires the
password**, and passwordless logins have none. More PAM cannot fix this.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**THE FIX** (in the dotfiles repo, deployed by `system/deploy`):
`system/etc/systemd/system/user@60006.service.d/10-home.conf` → `Environment=HOME=/home/sauyon`.
`Environment=` takes precedence over the `User=`-derived HOME — verified with
`sudo systemd-run --wait --pipe -p User=sauyon -p Environment=HOME=/tmp/hometest
sh -c 'echo $HOME'` → `/tmp/hometest`. This makes the search path correct from the first
instant regardless of mount state; if the manager still starts pre-unlock the path is
right but empty, and a later `systemctl --user daemon-reload` picks up every unit instead
of needing a full logout. Only takes effect on the next start of `user@60006.service`
(full logout of all sessions, or reboot).

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Also presents as **`home-manager switch` failing**: activation aborts at
`Activating sops-nix` with "Failed to restart sops-nix.service: Unit sops-nix.service
not found", which **silently skips every later activation step** (on utsuho:
`opencodeConfig`, `patchOpencodeModelStats`, `reloadSystemd`) — so `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
keeps its stale/unkeyed contents. Recover without logging out (verified 2026-07-31):

1. Render the secrets by running the unit's `ExecStart` by hand with a clean env —
   `env -i HOME=/home/sauyon USER=sauyon XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60006
   GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json PATH=
   $(grep ExecStart= <the sops-nix.service unit> | cut -d= -f2-)`.
   It bumps `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d/<n>` and repoints `~/.config/sops-nix/secrets`.
2. Run the skipped tail of `$(readlink -f ~/.local/state/nix/profiles/home-manager)/activate`
   under `bash` (not zsh — the script uses bash arrays) with `DRY_RUN_CMD=` and a stub
   `_iNote`. Skip `reloadSystemd`; it is a no-op while the manager is poisoned.

Workaround for GUI units (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
To recover the *current* boot: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service`
restarts with the home mounted. (The drop-in above prevents recurrence but cannot repair
a manager that is already running.)

content.text:
You're right — `HOME=/` is explicit homed configuration, and my "systemd falls back when the home is unusable" framing was wrong.

## What's actually happening

`docs/USER_RECORD.md` documents `useFallback`: when a login can't release the disk encryption key, homed flips `useFallback: true` and `fallbackHomeDirectory`/`fallbackShell` **override** the real ones. Your record has `fallbackHomeDirectory: "/"` literally. The stated purpose is to let "subsystems such as SSH" log into an account whose home needs further unlocking.

And it's definitely not a generic missing-home fallback — I tested: systemd sets `HOME=/usr/share/empty` for user `passim`, a directory that doesn't exist.

## Where the real defect is

`useFallback` is scoped to a **login session**. But that same login starts `user@60006.service`, which is **boot-scoped** — so a deliberately-degraded per-login value gets baked into a long-lived service and is never re-evaluated when `useFallback` flips back to `false`. That's a known open upstream bug: [systemd#30727](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/30727) (labels `homed` + `pid1`, still open) and [#36769](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/36769) (closed as dup of #34151).

## So is my drop-in wrong?

It's a workaround against an intentional mechanism, which I should have said. Two things make it narrower than it looks:

1. `Environment=` on `user@60006.service` only sets the **manager's** env. A locked SSH login still gets `fallbackShell` (`/usr/bin/systemd-home-fallback-shell` → `homectl`) from its own session lookup and can still unlock — the fallback UX is intact.
2. While locked, `/home/sauyon` doesn't exist and `/home` is root-owned `0755`, so nothing can write into a path that later gets shadowed. Pinning HOME degrades to the same "writes fail" as `/`.

Memory corrected. But it's your call whether to keep an override of a deliberate mechanism.

Agreed — and it turns out **OpenSSH on utsuho is already configured to do exactly that.** Tailscale SSH is the only thing bypassing it.

```
UsePAM                        yes
PasswordAuthentication        yes
AuthorizedKeysCommand         /usr/bin/userdbctl ssh-authorized-keys %u
KbdInteractiveAuthentication  no
```

`sshd` is enabled and active. So over OpenSSH, while your home is locked:

1. Pubkey auth **fails** — `authorized_keys` lives in the encrypted home, and your record has **0** `sshAuthorizedKeys`
2. It falls through to password → `UsePAM yes` → `pam_systemd_home.so` **auth** runs
3. That unlocks the home *before* logind creates the session
4. `user@60006.service` then starts with the real home. Nothing gets poisoned.

That is precisely the behavior you're describing, and it already works. Tailscale SSH registers straight with logind over D-Bus and never touches PAM ([#13198](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/13198)), so it can't participate — and it exposes no knob to change that.

**One trap to avoid:** don't "fix" this by putting your keys in the user record via `homectl update --ssh-authorized-keys=`. That would make pubkey auth *succeed* while the home is locked, which creates the session without unlocking — reproducing the exact bug through OpenSSH. The current failure-to-password path is what saves you.

I've left the drop-in in place as a safety net since you didn't ask me to revert it.

I'm not going to flip `--ssh` myself — that's your remote access, and if OpenSSH-over-tailnet doesn't work from some device you'd be locked out.

**Next (~2 min):** from another machine, confirm plain OpenSSH over the tailnet works — `ssh sauyon@100.x.y.z` (utsuho's tailnet IP) and check you get a password prompt. If that's clean, `tailscale set --ssh=false` removes the trigger and you get the prompt-then-unlock flow you want.

Want me to draft the upstream report against [tailscale#13198](https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/13198) with utsuho's evidence? I'd show it to you before anything is posted.

# Watch for sauyon's systemd-homed LUKS home to become available.
#
# Companion to user@60006.service.d/10-home.conf. That drop-in guarantees the user
# manager's unit search path is /home/sauyon/.config/systemd/user even when the manager
# is started by a passwordless login (Tailscale SSH, etc.) before the home is unlocked.
# But at that moment the directory does not exist yet, so the first scan finds nothing.
#
# This path unit fires the instant the directory appears -- i.e. whenever the home is
# unlocked, by ANY route: Tailscale SSH landing in homed's fallbackShell and typing the
# password, a physical login, or a manual `homectl activate`. The service it triggers
# makes the already-running user manager rescan, so every home-manager unit comes up
# without a logout and without Tailscale having to change anything.
#
# systemd watches the deepest existing ancestor and walks down as components appear, so
# a fully absent /home/sauyon is fine. Re-arms automatically if the home is deactivated.
[Unit]
Description=Watch for sauyon's homed home to be mounted

[Path]
PathExists=/home/sauyon/.config/systemd/user
Unit=sauyon-user-units-rescan.service

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

# Triggered by sauyon-user-units-rescan.path once /home/sauyon is mounted.
#
# Poke sauyon's already-running systemd user manager so it picks up the unit files that
# only became readable when the encrypted home was unlocked:

#                        manager skipped when it reached default.target with an empty
#                        search path
#
# Both are idempotent: on a normal physical login the manager is already healthy and
# default.target is already active, so this is a no-op. ExecStart is prefixed with `-`

# nothing to poke -- it will start later with a mounted home and be correct anyway.

After=home-sauyon.mount

RemainAfterExit=no
ExecStart=-/usr/bin/systemctl --machine=sauyon@.host --user daemon-reload
ExecStart=-/usr/bin/systemctl --machine=sauyon@.host --user start default.target

# Both are idempotent: on a normal physical login the manager is already healthy and
